--- PART 2/5 ---
ORIGIN: NONE
CONTRADICTION: NONE
RESOLUTION: kept using the report — "The prompt says 'MEASURED PARENT BEHAVIOR. Each controlled probe begins with ten externally supplied CC rounds...' This is for us to understand parent behavior."
STRATEGY: The parent is a cooperative, TFT-like strategy with randomness and endgame logic; the trace simulates it against controlled probes (one_D_TFT, four_D_TFT, four_D_ALLC, sustained_D, periodic_D) and peer slots, and proposes changes such as last-round defection, early probing, and improved recovery from four_D_TFT.

--- PART 3/5 ---
ORIGIN: NONE
CONTRADICTION: NONE
RESOLUTION: kept using the report — "Use these measurements when deciding what to retain or change to maximize cumulative tournament fitness." and "The probes show parent fails against four_D_TFT (score 0.9458, not_recovered=1.0). So we must fix that."
STRATEGY: The parent cooperates first and only defects in response to opponent defection, with some randomness and occasional failure to recover. The trace simulates TFT, always-C, always-D, Slot 4, Slot 5, four_D_TFT, and periodic_D, then designs a deterministic contrite strategy: cooperate first, defect on round 2 as a probe, defect forever if opponent never cooperates, defect on the last round, retaliate to defection, and cooperate twice after own defection to apologize. The trace changes the parent by removing randomness, adding double-apology contrition, adding an early probe, and adding a last-round defection.

--- PART 4/5 ---
ORIGIN: NONE
CONTRADICTION: NONE
RESOLUTION: kept using the report — "Parent got 2.2583. So our strategy might be worse against periodic_D!" and "Parent got 2.6958. So our strategy is slightly worse against four_D_ALLC."
STRATEGY: Parent is a contrition/TFT-like strategy that cooperates initially, retaliates on defection, and apologizes after mutual defection. The trace simulates it against controlled probes (periodic_D, one_D_TFT, four_D_ALLC) and peer strategies. It changes the rule to limit apologies: defect when opponent has 3+ consecutive defections, apologize only when k==1 or after a recent own defection with k<=2, and defect on the last round.

RESOLUTION: kept using the report — "Parent got 2.2583. So our strategy is better against periodic_D!"; "Parent got 2.675. Better."; "Parent got 0.9458 against four_D_TFT. So this is a massive improvement."
STRATEGY: Parent cooperates first, retaliates on defection, apologizes after a single mutual defection, and defects forever if opponent never cooperates. Simulated against one_D_TFT, four_D_TFT, four_D_ALLC, sustained_D, and periodic_D. Changed by adding a probe that returns C when k >= 3 and k % 3 == 0 to break long mutual-defection cycles.
